title: FHIR Ready | NHSN | CDC
content: Preparing Your Facility for Reporting FHIR Digital Quality Measures (dQMs) to NHSN Print Minus Related Pages AT A GLANCE Prepare Stakeholders : Engage key personnel at your facility for the transition to reporting digital quality measures (dQMs) using Healthcare Level Seven International (HL7®) Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources® (FHIR®). Appoint a Coordinator : Appoint a staff member to serve as the NHSN dQM Implementation Coordinator to oversee reporting tasks. Task Guide : Use this page as a resource to prepare for reporting dQMs to NHSN and for compliance tasks. On This Page Preparing to Report dQMs to NHSN Early Adopters NHSN dQM Implementation Coordinator Additional Information Preparing to Report dQMs to NHSN As part of the Digital Measure Reporting Plan, the facility will authorize NHSNLink to retrieve data from the designated health system-level FHIR application programming interfaces (APIs) to support transmission and calculation of digital quality measures (dQM s) to NHSN. This process follows established data governance protocols and ensures alignment with privacy and security standards. To submit FHIR digital quality measures (dQMs) to NHSN via NHSNLink, facilities must ensure their data comply with NHSN’s requirements as specified in the CDC NHSN dQM Content Package IG . Facilities should identify personnel who will serve as the champions or liaisons throughout preparation and implementation. These staff ensure the facility completes the necessary tasks before initial connection with NHSNLink and support the facility’s FHIR connection throughout the reporting process. NHSN will update this list of tasks periodically as we prepare for fully automated data exchange with healthcare facilities. Early Adopters NHSN will soon expand voluntary submission of FHIR-based digital quality measure (dQM) data beyond pilot facilities participating in the NHSN CoLab . Early Adopter facilities will be invited to voluntarily submit dQM data to NHSN to help test data submission functionality and analytic reports within the application, and to identify training and support needs prior to broader national expansion. Facilities interested in becoming Early Adopters are encouraged to check their FHIR readiness in advance. Check Your FHIR Readiness Facilities can check their FHIR R4 API conformance to US Core v6.1.0 , which serves as the baseline for the NHSN FHIR Implementation Guide. Recommended validation tool: Use the Inferno US Core Test Kit and run the test suite “US Core Server v6.1.0.” How to get started: Go to the Inferno US Core Test Kit Select Test Suite: “ US Core Server v6.1.0. ” Execute the tests against your production-like FHIR R4 endpoint and resolve any failures before starting NHSN dQM reporting. Important privacy note: Inferno on HealthIT.gov is a public demonstration environment provided by ONC and is not approved for sensitive data/PHI ; use synthetic test data and/or run Inferno locally for internal testing. More information about becoming an early adopter for NHSN dQMs will be released later in 2026. NHSN dQM Implementation Coordinator The NHSN dQM Implementation Coordinator is crucial for the success of the facility’s health system in this effort. This individual will: Coordinate with the NHSN Facility Administrator for submission of FHIR dQMs to NHSN. Serve as an educator for key personnel at the facility involved with reporting FHIR dQMs to NHSN Ensure the IT team is aware of and has implemented Key Action Items for Reporting FHIR dQMs to NHSN [PDF – 85 MB] . Share feedback with NHSN about the facility’s experience in implementing reporting of FHIR dQMs to NHSN.
